title: Ledger Posting Standard: Each Deficiency Balance Account Resolved on Its Own
content:
**Standard.** Each Deficiency Balance Account is resolved on its own: a payment posts only to the account the payer names, a plan or settlement offer covers exactly one account, and two accounts of the same borrower are never combined into one plan or one settlement amount. A deficiency payment never reduces a balance on an open contract, and a contract payment never reduces a deficiency balance. Broken arrangements are counted per account.

## Counting broken arrangements in the rolling 12 months

The broken arrangements of an account in the rolling 12 months are the arrangement offers of that account (plans and settlements) with the status broken whose broken date falls within the rolling 12 months ending today. The window runs back to the same calendar day 12 months earlier, that day itself excluded; where that calendar day does not exist in the earlier month, the last day of that month is used. The count is taken for the one account only; a broken arrangement on another account of the same borrower never enters it.

## The standard by posting

| Posting | Where it goes | Where it never goes |
|---|---|---|
| A payment on a deficiency account | The account the payer names | Another deficiency account; any open contract |
| A plan or settlement offer | Exactly one account | Two accounts together |
| A contract payment | The contract | Any deficiency balance |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A borrower holds two Deficiency Balance Accounts and pays one sum naming the first account. The whole payment posts to the first account; the second is unaffected.
- A borrower with two accounts asks for one plan for both. Each account is planned, or settled, on its own; no single plan amount or settlement amount covers both.
- Today is the 20th of a month. An arrangement of the account broken on the 21st of the same month a year earlier is inside the rolling 12 months; one broken on the 20th of that month a year earlier is outside it.
